title: LOUISVILLE FALL HARVEST FESTIVAL
full_story:
The 75th Annual Louisville Fall Harvest Festival will start one week from tomorrow.

Orders for Louisville Chamber of Commerce whole smoked pork loins can be purchased until Sunday, with pork loins to be picked up at Salt & Strings Butchery on November 10th from 4 to 7 pm.

The Kiddie Parade kicks things off at 2 pm, with Full Armor Christian School serving treats at the old Soda Fountain and the Red Brush Christian Church will be serving apple cider and the Louisville Christian Church will be serving free water near the pocket park.  From 4 to 6 pm the Methodist Church will be offering free chili with Das-zle Dance and tumble performing at 5:30 pm.  From 5:30 to 6:30 pm will be the past Queen reception at the State Bank Suite.  At 6:15 pm Sylvia and Meila Robey will sing on stage.  The Little Miss, JR Miss, and Queen pageants will be held at 7:00 pm.  There are 6 contestants vying for the title of Louisville Fall Festival Queen, The current Queen is Mila Zink.  There are 7 contestants in the JR Miss contest, the current JR Miss is Elsie Anderson, and there are 10 young ladies vying for the Little Miss title held by Landrey Eade.

The glow 5K walk, run will take place after the pageants.  From 9 to 10 pm there will be music on the square with Seth Schnautz.

Saturday starts with the Rotary Pancake breakfast at 7 am, with tickets now on sale.  The FFA, AG Mechanics Tractor show will be on the east side of the square and kids activities will start at 8 am and the Clay County Genealogical Society Library will have an open house.  The Clay County Cruisers Car Show begins at 9, there will also be a greased pig contest, sponsored by the Hoosier Prairie Baptist Church, and a country store will open at the old Clay County Jail with free coffee and popcorn.

The Princess pageant will be on the main stage at 10 am with special guest Briley Mullins performing.  Starting at 11 am will be the Chili Cook Off Contest, hosted by the North Clay FCCLA and the Louisville Chamber of Commerce, with tastings available to 1 pm.  Contestants should bring their chili to the pocket park by 10:45 am.  Sign up by emailing [email protected], the winner will get a $50 prize.  At 11:30 Power and Grace Tumbling will perform on the main stage.  At 1 pm Deputy Trevin Smith and his K9 Chief will have a demonstration.  The parade is at 2 pm, Katrina Van Dyke has been named as the parade marshal.  Following the parade the crowning of the Queens and the Rotary Basket Raffle winners will be announced.

For the Parade floats, cars, tractors, bands and Queens will line up at the grade school, horses will line up at the city park, Louisville Queens and contestants will line up on Magnolia Street, and Emergency Services will line up at the high school.  Handicap parking for the parade will be available on the east side of the square.

All weekend there will be arts, and crafts, food vendors, basket raffle and inflatables for the kids.

In conjunction with the Fall Harvest Festival Red Brush Christian Church will have a Trunk or Treat on Wednesday, October 28th from 6 to 7:30 pm, and the Louisville American Legion will have a meat shoot on Sunday, November 1st at 11 am.

title: IECC BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The Illinois Eastern Community Colleges board of trustees met Tuesday night at Olney Central College to outline future finances, capital investments, and upcoming changes to employee benefits.

Chancellor Taylor introduced a new enrollment dashboard designed to improve how the district tracks performance and student trends.  He also updated the board on recent campus listening sessions with employees.

On the financial front, the district is looking at a potential financing framework of up to nine-point-two-five million dollars to fund future capital investments.  Capital needs include HVAC replacements and athletic facility improvements.  Official bonds have not yet been issued, with further consideration coming in November.

Trustees also reconciled upcoming health and dental insurance renewals for 2027.  While medical rates are rising 15% and dental plans almost 12%, the district will continue fully funding employee-only coverage under co-designated high-deductible plans, absorbing an extra $226,000 in annual costs.

In other action, the district approved an expenditure of nearly $57,000 dollars for 2 new Dell servers to update the district’s computer networks.  The board also reviewed the annual athletics report, which noted that the system served 450 student-athletes and awarded two-point-three-seven million dollars in athletic scholarships.

Key personnel updates included promoting Libby McVicker to dean of students and Jared Price to Program Director of Academic Advising.

The next regular IECC board meeting is scheduled for November 17th at Wabash Valley College in Mount Carmel.

title: LIHEAP AVAILABLE
full_story:
CEFS Economic Opportunity Corp, as administrator of the Energy Assistance Program in the counties of Clay, Christian, Effingham, Fayette, Montgomery, Moultrie and Shelby announced that funds are available to assist income-eligible households with their natural gas, propane and/or electric bills and furnace assistance for inoperable heating systems.

The program began taking applications on October 1st, for adults age 60 and over, individuals with a disability, families with children age 5 years and under, and households that are disconnected from their utilities, have a disconnection notice or have less than 25% in their propane tank.  All other income eligible households can start applying November 2nd.

Applications will be taken on a first-come, first-served basis through August 13th, of 2027, or until funding is exhausted.  Households that receive a one-time benefit may return during the program year for a Reconnection Assistance or Furnace Assistance benefits, if needed.

The program has expanded eligibility this year.  Households that are customers of Ameren Illinois, Liberty Utilities, City of Flora, Village of Louisville, Village of Clay City or Shelby Electric must be at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines to receive a benefit from LIHEAP.

The monthly income guidelines are as follows, one person can make up to $3,990 a month, two people can make up to $5,410, three people can make up to $6,830, and four people can make up to $8,250.

Households that are customers of all other utilities/energy vendors must be at or below 60% of the State Median Income to receive a benefit from LIHEAP.  The income guidelines for that are as follows, one person can make up to $3,441 a month, two people can make up to $4,500, three people can make up to $5,558, and four people can make up to $6,617.

Go to www.cefseoc.org or liheapillinois.com for the income limits for households with 5 members and more.

The Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) provides one-time benefits to income eligible homeowners and renters to help with energy bills and for reconnection of energy service.

The following documentation is required for all applications; Proof of gross income from all household members for the prior 30-day period beginning with the date of application.  For all customers new to LIHEAP, and/or for new household members of previous customers, proof of Social Security numbers (SSN) for all household members.  Individuals without an SSN or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) can still apply and CEFS Outreach offices will advise accordingly.  A copy of current heat and electric bills issued within the last 30 days.  Cash assistance is available for renters who can provide a copy of their lease/rental agreement showing their heating costs are included in the rent.  Other documents may be needed based on your household situation.  If you have questions regarding this, please call the office.

Appointments can be made by contacting the CEFS Clay County Outreach office at 835 West North Street in Flora the phone number is 618-662-4024.  The office is open Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

In order that no one is denied the opportunity to make an application they will continue to take applications in person or by phone.  Required documentation can be submitted in-person, mail or electronically.  If you require any special accommodation, please contact the local CEFS Outreach office in your county to arrange.

Income eligible LIHEAP customers of Ameren Illinois will receive a monthly discount on their natural and/or electric bill through the Low-Income Discount Rates.  Visit powerbilldiscount.com to know more details.

title: TO ELECT 3 NEW MEMBERS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Agriculture (IDOA) announced an election will be held on Wednesday, for two board members in Illinois Wheat Development Board Districts, (IWDB) three and six as well as one statewide At-Large Board Member.  District six includes Clay, Wayne, Alexander, Edwards, Gallatin, Hamilton, Hardin, Johnson, Massac, Pope, Pulaski, Saline, Union, Wabash, White, Williamson Counties.  As no formal petitions were filed for these vacant board positions, producers of Illinois wheat residing in these Districts may participate in the Wednesday, election as a write-in candidate.  Producers must be of legal voting age, reside in the district for which they are running and be a qualified producer of wheat.  At-large write-in candidates may reside in any of the IWDB Districts.

Absentee ballots are available to those not available to vote in person by contacting IDOA at 217-524-1083 or by email at agr.marketnews.illinois.gov.  In-person voting will take place at the county Farm Bureau offices in Illinois during normal business hours.

For more information, call IDOA at (217) 524-1083 or the Illinois Wheat Association at (309) 557-3619.

title: SPRING REGISTRATION
full_story:
A new semester brings new opportunities, and Frontier Community College is inviting current and prospective students to take the next step toward their educational and career goals.  Spring registration is now underway for the Spring 2027 semester.

Whether you’re pursuing a degree, preparing to transfer to a four-year university, enhancing your workforce skills, or exploring a new interest, FCC offers affordable, high-quality educational opportunities designed to fit a variety of schedules and goals.

Students are encouraged to schedule an appointment with their advisor as soon as possible to discuss course options and build a schedule that supports their academic success.  The first day of Spring 2027 classes is January 11th.

Registration is open now, and early registration gives students the best selection of classes and course times.  For more information about Frontier Community College, call 618-842-3711 or visit iecc.edu/fcc.

Frontier Community College, located in Fairfield, Illinois, is part of Illinois Eastern Community Colleges and is committed to providing accessible, affordable, and high-quality educational opportunities that empower students and strengthen communities.

title: HARVEST FUEL RELIEF PROGRAM
full_story:
The US Agriculture Department will make $8 billion in payments to farmers as part of a new Harvest Fuel Relief (HFR) program.

Similar to the Farmer Bridge Assistance program, the HFR program will provide simple, proportional support to farmers using a uniform formula to cover a portion of modeled losses during the 2026 crop year.  This national loss average will be based on Farm Service Agency (FSA) reported planted acres, Economic Research Service cost of production estimates, and World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates yields and prices.

The program aims to provide relief during temporary market disruptions and increased input costs.

The $8 billion in payments are authorized under the Commodity Credit Corporation (CCC) by the FSA.

Commodity-specific payment rates for Title I commodities will be released in November.  Payment methodology for other eligible commodities will be announced at a later date.

Crop insurance linkage will not be required for participation in the Harvest Fuel Relief program; however, USDA strongly urges producers to take advantage of the enhanced risk management tools included in the Working Families Tax Cuts Act to best protect against price risk and volatility in the future.

Producers of non-Title I commodities, including specialty crop growers and fishermen, are encouraged to provide data related to increased fuel costs to [email protected] for USDA’s consideration when determining payment rates.

Eligible producers are encouraged to create a Login.gov account in advance of the application period announcement.  Pre-filled applications will be available online to producers with a Login.gov account linked to USDA.

Earlier this year, the Farmer Bridge Assistance program delivered $12 billion in one-time bridge payments over 560,000 farmers across the country.

Many farmers could see a decline in net farm income in 2026 as rising production costs and weaker livestock markets outweigh gains in crop receipts, according to USDA’s latest farm income forecast.
